Configure a generic fishery capture model

Source: R/sim_capture.R
sim_capture.Rd

Returns a function for the catch_model argument of sim_fishery(). Capture proposals use a bounded encounter probability and an optional gear capacity.

sim_capture(q, capacity_per_gear = Inf)

Arguments

q

Nonnegative capture coefficient, in grid-area units per gear-time unit. It can exceed one; it is not a capture probability.

capacity_per_gear

Maximum fish per gear unit in one operation, or Inf.

Value

A function with arguments available and operation. available is a table with age, length, N, selectivity, and cell_area; operation includes gear_amount, duration, and effort, plus identifiers/location. The function returns one nonnegative whole-fish proposal per available row.

Details

For gear amount G, duration T, selectivity s, and cell area A, the probability is 1 - exp(-q * G * T * s / A). Binomial proposals are sampled from the available age-length counts. If necessary, proposals are sampled without replacement to respect floor(capacity_per_gear * G). This is an idealized encounter-and-capacity model, not a mechanistic model of every gear's soak-time response. Alternative capture functions may be supplied. The symbol q is conventional in fisheries catch/effort models; see https://www.fao.org/4/x5685e/x5685e04.htm. It differs from the dimensionless age/length catchability probabilities supplied as q to sim_survey().

Examples

capture <- sim_capture(q = 0.1, capacity_per_gear = 1)
available <- data.frame(age = 1:2, length = c(10, 20), N = c(100, 50),
                        selectivity = c(0.5, 1), cell_area = 25)
capture(available, list(gear_amount = 10, duration = 4, effort = 40))
#> [1] 8 2
